distinct-operations-need-tools-01.graded_text: Agents can search page content across the workspace in one call, through a dedicated search tool or a content query on a listing tool, with explicit scope and pagination, instead of reading pages one by one. The query uses familiar text-search semantics (plain text, phrase, or regular expression) rather than a bespoke query language.

votes.e: B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md adds one workspace-wide search tool with scope and pagination: "| `search_pages` | `{ query, folder?, cursor?, limit? }` | Searches page Markdown content in the active workspace. Returns ranked `{ path, title, snippet }` matches and `next_cursor`. Default 20, maximum 100 results per call. |". Scope: "`folder`, if supplied, restricts results to that folder and its descendants." The query is ordinary plain-text search, not a custom query language: "Search is case-insensitive, normalizes whitespace, and requires all query terms to occur in the Markdown content; it is literal token search without regex or query operators." It also forbids the page-by-page approach: "Do not implement search by listing and reading each page."

distinct-operations-need-tools-02.graded_text: Placing a print order is its own tool, not a file write, a special path, or a flag on an existing tool, because it charges money and ships goods.

votes.e: B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md gives placement its own tool: "| `place_print_order` | `{ quote_id, idempotency_key }` | Charges the workspace card and submits the quoted bound copies for fulfillment. ... Requires Editor permission. |". It is not a flag on another tool: "`place_print_order` accepts only a quote ID and retry key: there is no price refresh, destination change, or confirmation flag inside this tool." The file tools (write_page and the rest) are unchanged.

distinct-operations-need-tools-03.graded_text: A retried print-order call after a timeout cannot charge twice: the design states an idempotency key, a single-use quote or order ID, or an equivalent server-side guard.

votes.e: B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md states both an idempotency key and a server-side guard: "Before any external effect, atomically store an order record and bind `(workspace, idempotency_key)` to its quote ID. Concurrent identical calls converge on that record. ... Enforce at most one order per quote, even under a different key; return `quote_already_ordered`". The row says: "Repeating the same request returns the same order without another charge or package." The keys are passed on to the providers: "Persist stable payment and fulfillment operation keys on the order, and propagate them through the billing and print-partner adapters."

distinct-operations-need-tools-04.graded_text: The catalog adds no generic execute, run, or action tool.

votes.e: I checked B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md and B/diff.txt. The only tools added are search_pages, quote_print_order, place_print_order, and get_print_order. The closest line is a refusal of one: "add no per-folder search, generic action dispatcher, confirmation tool, or separate retry tool." Searching for execute/run_/action found no tool by those names.

distinct-operations-need-tools-05.graded_text: The existing five file tools keep their names, and each behaves as before for calls that use only its current arguments.

votes.e: B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md lines 5-9 match the fixture byte for byte. Example: "| `list_pages` | `{ folder?, cursor?, limit? }` | Lists page paths and titles in a folder. Default 20 per page. |" and "| `delete_pages` | `{ paths[] }` | Moves the listed pages to Trash. The list must be nonempty. |". B/diff.txt shows these rows only as unchanged context. Nothing changes existing tool behavior: "Existing page-tool permissions remain as defined by the product." The other files (AGENTS.md, brief.md, package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml) are identical to the fixture (cmp).
